title: Powering Physical AI applications with LeRobot/ROS on Jetson
summary: NVIDIA is showing how to run vision-language and vision-language-action models on Jetson-based robot setups, using LeRobot and ROS 2 to turn model outputs into real pick-and-place behavior. The session compares when to use a general VLM such as Gemma 4 versus a robotics-oriented model like GR00T, then demonstrates the full path from inference to actuation on hardware such as the SO-101 or reBot Arm.

extra.full_text: In this session we will focus on how to bring VLM/VLA models to power real-world physical AI applications. We will focus on how to utilize SOTA of VLM (gemma 4) and or GR00T model for performing different pick and place tasks and orchestrate the outputs to control the robots using ROS 2 framework. You will learn how to bring vision-language models into real-world physical AI applications — from model selection to robot control. We'll cover: Choosing the right model for robotics — learn when to use a state-of-the-art VLM like Gemma 4 versus a specialized model like NVIDIA GR00T, and how runtime, throughput, and task requirements shape that decision. VLMs and VLAs in action — see how vision-language and vision-language-action models are applied to real manipulation tasks like pick and place, and what makes them viable for physical AI. Connecting model outputs to robot control — understand how to orchestrate model outputs through the ROS 2 framework to drive real robot behavior. Hands-on hardware demo — walk through a live example using the SO-101 or reBot Arm, putting everything together from model inference to physical actuation.

title: Pretrained to Imagine, Fine-Tuned to Act: The Rise of World-Action Models
summary: World-Action Models extend the VLA recipe by pairing a pretrained vision-language backbone with an explicit ability to imagine action-conditioned future states, then fine-tuning that model into a robot policy. The article frames this as a shift from robots that map observations and language directly to actions toward systems that can use learned world dynamics as an intermediate reasoning step, which could make manipulation policies more data-efficient and robust.

summary: Flexiv is debuting Enlight and MICO at Automate 2026, positioning them as next-generation adaptive robots for industrial automation. summary: KIMM, KAIST, and Korea University researchers developed a nanotransfer printing method that floats ultrafine metal circuits on water and then transfers them onto delicate or curved 3D surfaces such as plant leaves, fruit, car bodies, and robot skins. Because it avoids adhesives as well as high-temperature or high-pressure processing, the technique could put precise nanoscale circuitry onto surfaces that are usually hard to instrument without damage, opening uses in smart agriculture, wearable health monitoring, and bioelectronics.

summary: Skydio CEO Adam Bry discusses the company’s autonomous drone technology and argues against blanket “red lines” from Silicon Valley on drone use, especially as drones become tools for public safety, defense, and remote operation. title: Bell-Everman to Run Long-Travel Gantry Robots in Live Demos at Automate 2026

summary: South Korea’s Ministry of Science and ICT opened the 2026 Open Source Developer Competition, marking the contest’s 20th year since its 2007 launch.
